rubric.why: Identifies what a system is and the purpose its parts share.
rubric.description: A system is a collection of parts that work together toward a common goal.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark when the answer identifies a collection of parts working together for a shared goal; all three ideas are required (equivalent wording accepted).

rubric.why: Names the four elements used to describe a system.
rubric.description: A system is described by its objectives, components, communication among components, and working environment.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark when all four elements are named; equivalent wording for communication among components or the environment is accepted.

modelAnswer: A system is a collection of parts that work together to achieve a common goal. A system is described by its objectives components, communication among components and environment in which it works.

rubric.why: Identifies memory and the central processing unit as two primary components.
rubric.description: The primary components include memory and the CPU.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming both memory and the CPU (Central Processing Unit).

rubric.why: Identifies both input and output components.
rubric.description: The primary components include input mechanisms and output mechanisms.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming both input and output mechanisms or devices.

modelAnswer: The Von Neumann architecture has four primary components: the memory, the Central Processing Unit (CPU), input mechanisms, and output mechanisms.

rubric.why: Defines the architecture as a computer paradigm or system with four primary hardware components.
rubric.description: The Von Neumann architecture is a computer paradigm describing hardware with four primary components.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying it as a computer paradigm or system and stating that the hardware has four primary components.

rubric.description: The four components are memory, CPU, input devices, and output devices.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark when all four components are named; equivalent terms for the CPU and input/output devices are accepted.

modelAnswer: The Von Neumann architecture is a computer paradigm that delineates a system in which the hardware of the computer has four primary components: the memory, the Central Processing Unit (CPU), input mechanisms, and output mechanisms.
The key components are memory, CPU, input devices, and output devices.

rubric.why: Identifies fetching and decoding, including their essential actions.
rubric.description: Fetching retrieves an instruction from memory; decoding is performed by the Control Unit.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for both stages: retrieving an instruction from memory and decoding it with the Control Unit (CU).

rubric.why: Identifies execution and storing, including the result destination.
rubric.description: Execution processes the instruction; storing sends the result to memory or an output device.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for both stages: the CPU processes the instruction, and the result is returned to memory or sent to an output device.

modelAnswer: Fetching: The central processing unit retrieves an instruction from the computer’s memory. Decoding: The Control Unit (CU) decodes the instruction.
Execution: The CPU processes the instruction. Storing: The outcome of the computation is either returned to memory or sent to an output device.

rubric.why: Identifies the single memory area as the limiting factor.
rubric.description: The bottleneck occurs because of a single memory area.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the bottleneck involves one or a single memory area.

rubric.why: Explains that this limits how quickly the CPU can retrieve both instructions and data.
rubric.description: The memory area limits the CPU’s retrieval speed for instructions and data.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that CPU retrieval of instructions and data is limited or slowed.

modelAnswer: The Von Neumann bottleneck occurs when a single memory area limits the CPU's ability to retrieve instructions and data quickly.

rubric.why: Identifies flexibility or the ability to change programs as the advantage.
rubric.description: The architecture is flexible because programs can be changed.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying flexibility or stating that programs can be changed.

rubric.why: States how the programs are changed.
rubric.description: Programs are changed by changing the contents of memory.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that the program changes when memory contents are changed.

modelAnswer: Flexibility: Programs can be easily changed by changing memory contents.
